source.original_text: The actual precision–matrix reply is the genuine Euclidean gradient and determines the centered quadratic value. \nabla f_A(x)=Ax,\qquad f_A(x)=\tfrac12\langle x,Ax\rangle. \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Fix any full real \(O\in O(d)\), allowing either determinant sign, and every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). For \(i=1,\ldots,d\), set \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and \(A=A_\kappa=O\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)O^\top\). The Lean index \(j\in\mathrm{Fin}(d)\) represents \(i=j.\mathrm{val}+1\). The potential is exactly \(f_A(x)=x^\top Ax/2\), with zero additive constant. The response is exact precision multiplication \(q_A(x)=Ax\), not covariance multiplication \(A^{-1}x\) or the primitive hidden-rotation response \(Ox\). The proof produces actual Fréchet derivative existence at every point, then identifies Lean’s total \(\mathrm{gradient}\). Differentiability, symmetry, admissibility, a gradient certificate and reply correctness are not added assumptions. The private consumer uses the same hidden \(O\) for \(A_2\) and \(A_\kappa\). It reconstructs \(g=(\kappa-1)A_2x-(\kappa-2)x\), then the actual pair \((\langle x,g\rangle/2,g)\). Reference \(2\) is the condition-number parameter. The selected direction has no reciprocal or inverse-reply premise. This is pointwise in the latent matrix; the mathematical parameter \(O\) is not an algorithmic disclosure of the eigenbasis. Random seeds, Haar laws, adaptive transcripts, query budgets and sampling accuracy are outside this statement.

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every natural number d, with an explicit proof argument hd witnessing 2 ≤ d; for every real number κ, with an explicit proof argument hκ witnessing 2 ≤ κ; and for every matrix O in the full real orthogonal group on the d coordinates, make the following local definitions.

The coordinate indices are i ∈ Fin d, with natural values i.val = 0, …, d − 1. Set
  θ(i) = ((i.val as a real number) + 1/2) π / (d as a real number),
  A = O diag(i ↦ (κ + 1)/2 + ((κ − 1)/2) cos(θ(i))) Oᵀ.
Let E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), identified with ℝ^d with its usual real Euclidean inner product. Define, for x ∈ E,
  f(x) = ((WithLp.ofLp x) · (A (WithLp.ofLp x))) / 2,
  query(x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (A (WithLp.ofLp x)).
The maps WithLp.ofLp and WithLp.toLp 2 preserve the vector coordinates, so these formulas say f(x) = xᵀAx/2 and query(x) = Ax in ordinary coordinates. The orthogonality assumption is OᵀO = OOᵀ = I and permits either determinant sign.

Then for every x ∈ E both of the following assertions hold:
1. HasGradientAt f (query(x)) x: f is genuinely real Fréchet differentiable at x, with derivative the linear functional h ↦ ⟨query(x), h⟩, for h ∈ E.
2. The ordered-pair identity
     (f(x), gradient f x) = (⟨x, query(x)⟩ / 2, query(x))
   holds.

Here gradient f x denotes the inverse Riesz image of the totalized real Fréchet derivative fderiv ℝ f x, with the stated zero fallback where a derivative does not exist. Assertion 1 is an explicit conjunct, so assertion 2 is accompanied by genuine differentiability at the same x. The symbols θ, A, f, and query are the local definitions above, not additional universally quantified inputs. E is only explanatory notation for the displayed Euclidean space, and h is bound only within the derivative description.

/-!
# Actual fixed-spectrum first-order replies

Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1, Section2 Equation1, Section4.1
Equation11 and the ordinary quadratic-calculus meaning in AppendixC.4.
For the literal cosine-grid precision and every full real orthogonal O,
the exact precision-matvec reply is the genuine Euclidean gradient.
Derivative existence is produced before identifying the total gradient.
The actual centered potential value is recovered from that same reply.

The focused Test combines this result with the identical canonical same-O
affine precision provider. No operational query count, adaptive transcript,
Gaussian target/TV, finite-precision or expected-cost transport is asserted.
The remaining C4 regularity/minimizer and both main bounds are separate.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumFirstOrder

theorem actual_first_order_query {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
        Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
      (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
    let query : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) :=
      fun x => WithLp.toLp 2 (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      HasGradientAt f (query x) x ∧
      (f x, gradient f x) = (inner ℝ x (query x) / 2, query x) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
    (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
      Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
  let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
    (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
  let query : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) :=
    fun x => WithLp.toLp 2 (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let H : E →L[ℝ] E := Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d) A
  -- The actual family's existing canonical producer supplies symmetry.
  have hA : A.IsHermitian :=
    (FixedSpectrumAdmissibility.actual_precision_admissible hd hκ O).1.1
  have hself : IsSelfAdjoint A := hA
  have hH : H.IsSymmetric :=
    ContinuousLinearMap.isSelfAdjoint_iff_isSymmetric.mp
      (hself.map (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d)))
  have hquery (x : E) : query x = H x := rfl
  have hf : f = fun y : E => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * inner ℝ y (H y) := by
    funext y
    dsimp only [f]
    rw [show inner ℝ y (H y) = (WithLp.ofLp y) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp y) from
      Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM A y y]
    ring
  -- Differentiate the actual function and identify its Riesz functional.
  have hgrad (y : E) : HasGradientAt f (H y) y := by
    have hraw := ((hasFDerivAt_id y).inner ℝ H.hasFDerivAt).const_mul (1 / 2 : ℝ)
    have hlin : (1 / 2 : ℝ) •
        ((fderivInnerCLM ℝ (y, H y)).comp ((ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E).prod H)) =
        toDual ℝ E (H y) := by
      ext v
      change (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (inner ℝ y (H v) + inner ℝ v (H y)) = inner ℝ (H y) v
      rw [← hH.apply_clm y v, (real_inner_comm v (H y)).symm]
      ring
    apply hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr
    rw [hf, ← hlin]
    exact hraw
  intro x
  have hg : HasGradientAt f (query x) x := (hquery x).symm ▸ hgrad x
  refine ⟨hg, Prod.ext ?_ hg.gradient⟩
  change f x = inner ℝ x (query x) / 2
  rw [hquery]
  exact congrArg (fun t : ℝ => t / 2) (Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM A x x).symm

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumFirstOrder

steps.title: Obtain symmetry of the actual precision
steps.text: Use the existing canonical admissibility result for this literal source matrix. Its positive-definite output supplies Hermitian symmetry internally; no regularity certificate is assumed.
steps.lean: hA is the Hermitian projection of actual_precision_admissible hd hκ O. Mapping self-adjointness through Matrix.toEuclideanCLM gives hH. This one existing actual admissibility declaration is the sole direct ASTIS producer parent.

steps.title: Identify the same Euclidean quadratic
steps.text: The matrix action and the continuous linear map have identical coordinates. The ordinary coordinate dot product therefore agrees with the Euclidean inner product for the same potential.
steps.lean: hquery is the actual coordinate-preserving map identity. Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM and real ring algebra establish hf, without changing f or introducing an additive constant.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual function
steps.text: Differentiate the identity map and the continuous linear map, then the inner product and multiplication by one half. This directly constructs a Fréchet derivative.
steps.lean: hraw uses hasFDerivAt_id, H.hasFDerivAt, the canonical inner-product derivative and const_mul. This is a derivative-existence proof, not an evaluation of a default gradient.

steps.title: Use symmetry to obtain the genuine gradient
steps.text: Symmetry makes the two derivative terms equal. The resulting derivative is exactly the Riesz functional associated with Hx, so the actual gradient exists and equals the response.
steps.lean: hlin identifies the continuous linear derivative with toDual of Hx, using hH and real_inner_comm. hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt produces hgrad; hg.gradient identifies the total gradient only after existence.

steps.title: Assemble the exact first-order reply
steps.text: Combine the proved gradient with the coordinate value identity. The same actual precision response determines both entries of the first-order observation.
steps.lean: Prod.ext combines the actual value equality with hg.gradient. The exact original source signature and all binders remain unchanged.

steps.title: Consume the actual reference-precision reply
steps.text: In the focused Test, the existing same-rotation affine provider converts the actual A2 reply into the actual Aκ action. Substitute it into the new derivative and pair results, giving the genuine observation of the κ potential.
steps.lean: The private Test actually invokes FixedSpectrumAffine.actual_affine_precision_query and the new actual_first_order_query. Its two direct kernel ASTIS parents are those exact canonical declarations. Only the forward affine output is consumed; no inverse/nonzero bridge, count assertion or extra producer premise is used.
